KARIOBANGI COLD STORAGE & LOGISTICS LIMITED
COMMERCIAL PROPERTY — FLOOD AND SPECIAL PERILS INSURANCE POLICY Insurer: Amani General Insurance Company Limited
Policy Number: AGI/FLD/2025/02116
Insured: Kariobangi Cold Storage & Logistics Limited
Risk Address: Plot 7, Outer Ring Road, Kariobangi South, Nairobi, Kenya
Occupancy/Use: Cold storage warehouse and distribution depot (foodstuffs, packaging, refrigerated plant)
Period of Insurance: 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2026
Hazard context (underwriting note): Risk sits within Nairobi Eastlands pluvial-flood corridors
identified in county hotspot lists (Kariobangi / Dandora / Njiru drainage catchment). Cover is
for pluvial and fluvial flood as defined below; catastrophe modelling for the book uses
susceptibility scores and return-period tiers consistent with Kenya Re Team A Nairobi flood desk. SECTION A: PROPERTY INSURED Item 1 - Buildings (cold rooms, loading bays, administration block, boundary walls) Sum Insured: KES 160,000,000 Item 2 - Plant and Machinery (refrigeration plant, generators, racking, material handling) Sum Insured: KES 95,000,000 Item 3 - Stock (frozen and chilled foodstuffs, packaging materials) Sum Insured: KES 125,000,000 Total Sum Insured: KES 380,000,000

SECTION B: PERILS COVERED This Policy covers loss or damage to the Property Insured caused by: 1. Flood — inundation of normally dry land by water from intense rainfall (pluvial), overflow of natural or artificial watercourses, or failure/overflow of public drainage within Nairobi County, including surface-water ponding 2. Storm and tempest 3. Escape of water from tanks, apparatus, or pipes (excluding gradual seepage) 4. Fire (limited extension — see Section C) 5. Lightning 6. Impact by vehicles 7. Riot, strike and malicious damage

SECTION C: EXCLUSIONS This Policy does not cover: 1. Loss or damage caused by the Insured's own wilful act or gross negligence. 2. Loss or damage arising from war, invasion, act of foreign enemy, civil war, or terrorism, unless specifically bought back by endorsement. 3. Loss or damage where the Insured has failed to maintain the flood-mitigation measures declared at inception (see Warranties 1 and 2 below). 4. Consequential loss, including loss of profits, business interruption, spoilage from refrigeration failure unless caused by an insured peril interrupting power for more than 12 continuous hours, or loss of market, unless separately insured. 5. Gradual damp, mould, or rising damp not attributable to a sudden flood event. 6. Loss or damage occurring while the premises are left unoccupied for a continuous period exceeding 30 days, unless declared and agreed by the Insurer in writing. 7. Fines, penalties, or punitive damages of any kind. 8. Loss discovered more than 30 days after the Insured first became aware, or ought reasonably to have become aware, of circumstances giving rise to a claim, unless late notification is excused in writing by the Insurer. 9. Damage to landscaping, unpaved yards, or temporary structures unless caused by an insured flood event and specifically scheduled.

SECTION D: WARRANTIES Warranty 1 (Drainage and Site Flood Defence Warranty): It is warranted that the
Insured shall, at all times during the currency of this Policy: (a) keep site drainage channels, culvert inlets, and the connection to the public storm-water system clear of silt, solid waste, and debris, with documented clearance at least once every 90 days during the long rains (March–May) and short rains (October–December); (b) maintain any declared sandbag stores, temporary barriers, or bund walls in usable condition before forecast heavy-rainfall alerts issued by the Kenya Meteorological Department for Nairobi County; (c) not obstruct or permanently alter drainage paths shown on the risk survey without prior written agreement of the Insurer.
Breach of this Warranty, if material to the cause or extent of the loss, entitles the
Insurer to decline or reduce indemnity in respect of the affected claim.

Warranty 2 (Elevated Storage / Flood-Mark Warranty): It is warranted that stock and
critical plant shall be stored or installed with the lowest storage tier or plant base
not less than 0.45 metres above the finished floor level of the main cold-room hall
(the "declared flood mark"), except for goods in active loading/unloading for not more
than 48 continuous hours. Breach of this Warranty, if material to the extent of stock
or plant loss, entitles the Insurer to decline or reduce indemnity for the affected items.

SECTION E: EXCESS/DEDUCTIBLE Each and every flood claim: KES 3,000,000, or 2.5% of the claim amount, whichever is greater.
Other insured perils: KES 2,000,000, or 2% of the claim amount, whichever is greater. SECTION F: CONDITIONS PRECEDENT TO LIABILITY 1. The Insured shall notify the Insurer within 14 days of any occurrence likely to give rise to a claim. 2. The Insured shall furnish all information and documentary evidence reasonably required by the Insurer, including invoices, stock records, rainfall/flood photographs, and drainage-maintenance logs. 3. The Insured shall take all reasonable steps to minimise or avert loss, including moving stock above the flood mark where safe to do so when flood warnings are issued for Eastlands / Outer Ring Road corridors. 4. No admission, offer, promise, or payment shall be made by or on behalf of the Insured without the written consent of the Insurer.

SECTION G: REINSURANCE NOTE (for internal cedant use) This risk is ceded under the Amani General Insurance Company Limited Flood and Special
Perils Surplus Treaty with Kenya Reinsurance Corporation Limited, Treaty Reference
KR/AGI/FLD/SUR/2026, subject to the terms of that treaty. Any claim under this Policy
exceeding the cedant's retention shall be notified to Kenya Reinsurance Corporation
Limited within 14 days of the cedant becoming aware of it. Signed for and on behalf of Amani General Insurance Company Limited.

KENYA REINSURANCE CORPORATION LIMITED
FLOOD AND SPECIAL PERILS SURPLUS REINSURANCE TREATY Treaty Reference: KR/AGI/FLD/SUR/2026
Reinsurer: Kenya Reinsurance Corporation Limited ("Kenya Re")
Cedant: Amani General Insurance Company Limited ("the Cedant")
Class of Business: Flood and Special Perils (Commercial and Industrial risks), with
emphasis on urban pluvial and fluvial flood exposures in the Republic of Kenya
Treaty Type: Surplus (proportional)
Period: 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2026, and each anniversary thereafter unless
terminated in accordance with Article 14. ARTICLE 1 - SCOPE This Treaty covers the Cedant's Flood and Special Perils portfolio written in the
Republic of Kenya, including warehousing, cold storage, manufacturing, commercial and
industrial occupancies exposed to storm, tempest, and flood (including Nairobi urban
pluvial inundation and drainage overflow), subject to the terms, conditions, limits
and exclusions set out below. Portfolio catastrophe views may reference Kenya Re's
Nairobi flood desk hazard tiers (return periods 5 / 10 / 25 / 100 / 250 years) for
underwriting context; such models do not amend the indemnity terms of this Treaty.

ARTICLE 2 - CEDANT'S RETENTION AND TREATY CAPACITY 2.1 The Cedant's retention (Line) for any one risk is KES 50,000,000 of Sum Insured.
2.2 The Treaty provides 8 Lines of automatic surplus capacity, being KES 400,000,000 in excess of the Cedant's retention, giving total automatic capacity of KES 450,000,000 per risk.
2.3 Kenya Re participates on each risk ceded in the same proportion as the surplus amount bears to the total Sum Insured of that risk (the "Cession Percentage").
2.4 Kenya Re's share of any claim is calculated by applying the Cession Percentage to the amount of the claim payable by the Cedant under the original Policy, after deduction of the Policy excess.

ARTICLE 3 - RISKS REQUIRING ENHANCED ASSESSMENT 3.1 Any risk with a total Sum Insured exceeding KES 300,000,000, or any risk located in a named Nairobi flood hotspot corridor (including but not limited to Kariobangi, Dandora, Mathare, Kibera, Kawangware, Kayole, Njiru, and Ruai as used on the Kenya Re Nairobi flood desk), shall be classified as an Enhanced Assessment Risk.
3.2 For Enhanced Assessment Risks, the Cedant shall, prior to binding cover, provide Kenya Re with: (a) a risk survey not older than 24 months addressing drainage and flood-mark storage; (b) confirmation of flood-mitigation measures in place; (c) loss history for the preceding 5 years; and (d) occupancy and construction details including housing/building vulnerability class where relevant.
3.3 Underwriting guideline reference: Section 4.2 of the Kenya Re Underwriting Manual requires that Enhanced Assessment Risks be reviewed by a Senior Underwriter before automatic cession is confirmed, and that any risk with Sum Insured exceeding KES 400,000,000 be referred for facultative consideration outside this Treaty.

ARTICLE 4 - EXCLUSIONS UNDER THE TREATY This Treaty excludes and Kenya Re shall have no liability in respect of: 4.1 War, invasion, act of foreign enemy, hostilities, civil war, rebellion, insurrection, or terrorism. 4.2 Nuclear risks of any kind. 4.3 Losses arising from the Cedant's failure to comply with a Warranty under the original Policy, where such failure is material to the loss. 4.4 Losses where the original Policy excess has not first been applied. 4.5 Business interruption or consequential loss, unless separately agreed by addendum to this Treaty. 4.6 Any risk bound by the Cedant in breach of the underwriting guidelines referenced in Article 3.3.

ARTICLE 5 - CLAIMS NOTIFICATION AND COOPERATION 5.1 The Cedant shall notify Kenya Re within 14 days of becoming aware of any claim or circumstance likely to involve this Treaty, and in any event immediately for any claim where the estimated gross loss exceeds KES 20,000,000.
5.2 The Cedant shall provide Kenya Re with all documentation reasonably required to assess the claim, including the claim form, original Policy, flood investigation or loss adjuster reports, stock records, photographs, drainage-maintenance logs, and any other supporting evidence.
5.3 Kenya Re shall be entitled to appoint its own loss adjuster, at its own cost, to review any claim where the Cedant's estimated gross loss exceeds KES 50,000,000, or where Kenya Re reasonably considers the claim to be unusual having regard to the Cedant's historical flood claims experience under this Treaty.
5.4 Claims shall be settled by the Cedant in accordance with the terms of the original Policy. Kenya Re shall follow the fortunes of the Cedant, provided that the claim has been handled by the Cedant in good faith and in accordance with the terms of the original Policy and this Treaty.

ARTICLE 6 - CLAIMS REQUIRING PRIOR REFERRAL TO KENYA RE 6.1 Notwithstanding Article 5.4, the Cedant shall obtain Kenya Re's prior written agreement before settling any claim where: (a) the estimated gross loss exceeds KES 60,000,000; or (b) there is a reasonable suspicion of fraud, material misrepresentation at inception, or deliberate obstruction of drainage; or (c) the cause of loss, or the applicability of a Policy exclusion or Warranty (including drainage and elevated-storage warranties), is genuinely in doubt; or (d) required documentation under the original Policy (including but not limited to flood investigation or loss adjuster reports, and drainage- maintenance records) has not yet been furnished.
6.2 Where none of the conditions in Article 6.1 apply, and the claim is otherwise consistent with the Cedant's normal flood claims experience, the Cedant may proceed to settle the claim without further reference to Kenya Re, subject to Article 5.2. ARTICLE 7 - PREMIUM AND COMMISSION Kenya Re shall receive its Cession Percentage of the original gross premium, less
a ceding commission of 30%, payable quarterly. ARTICLE 8 - CURRENCY All amounts under this Treaty are expressed in Kenya Shillings (KES) unless
otherwise stated.

ARTICLE 8 - CURRENCY All amounts under this Treaty are expressed in Kenya Shillings (KES) unless
otherwise stated. ARTICLE 9 - CATASTROPHE PROTECTION This Treaty operates net of the Cedant's own Catastrophe Excess of Loss
protection, where applicable. A single occurrence (including a continuous
rainfall/flood event defined as one occurrence under the Cedant's original
wording) affecting multiple risks ceded under this Treaty shall be aggregated
for the purposes of any such protection. Nairobi pluvial events affecting
multiple Eastlands locations in the same meteorological episode are treated as
one occurrence unless the Cedant's original policies define otherwise. ARTICLE 10 to 13 - [General conditions: arbitration, errors and omissions,
inspection of records, offset, taxation - standard treaty wording, on file with
both parties.] ARTICLE 14 - DURATION AND TERMINATION This Treaty renews annually unless either party gives not less than 3 months'
written notice prior to any anniversary date. Executed between the Cedant and Kenya Reinsurance Corporation Limited.

AMANI GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED
CLAIM FORM - FLOOD AND SPECIAL PERILS Claim Reference: AGI/CLM/2026/2048
Policy Number: AGI/FLD/2025/02116
Insured: Kariobangi Cold Storage & Logistics Limited
Risk Address: Plot 7, Outer Ring Road, Kariobangi South, Nairobi, Kenya 1. DETAILS OF LOSS Date of Loss: 14–15 April 2026 (overnight into early morning)
Time of Loss: Inundation first observed approximately 23:10 hrs on 14 April 2026;
peak water depth inside the main cold-room hall approximately 01:40 hrs on 15 April 2026
Date Reported to Insurer: 15 April 2026
Cause of Loss (as understood by Insured): Pluvial / urban flood following intense
rainfall over Nairobi Eastlands. Surface water entered from Outer Ring Road and the
blocked roadside drain adjoining the loading bay; water ponded across the yard and
entered the cold-room hall through loading-bay doors. Consistent with Kariobangi /
Dandora drainage-corridor flooding reported across neighbouring premises the same night. 2. DESCRIPTION OF INCIDENT

2. DESCRIPTION OF INCIDENT The night supervisor, Ms. Amina Otieno, reported water rising across the yard at
approximately 23:10 hrs and raised the internal alarm. Staff attempted to move
palletised stock onto higher racking and to sandbag the loading-bay doors, but water
entered faster than barriers could be placed. Peak depth inside the main hall was
estimated at 35–40 cm above finished floor level. Floodwater began to recede after
04:30 hrs on 15 April 2026 as rainfall eased and the county storm-water system
partially cleared. No fatalities were reported. Refrigeration plant shorted when
water reached motor bases in the plant room; backup generator was started but could
not restore full cold-chain capacity until electrical isolation was completed. 3. ITEMS/PROPERTY AFFECTED - Main cold-room hall: floodwater damage to lower racking, flooring, and wall panels - Loading bay and yard: silt, debris, and damaged roller-door seals - Stock on ground-level and first racking tiers: substantial spoilage / contamination - Refrigeration plant motors and switchgear at base level: water damage - Administration block: minor water ingress at entrance lobby only - Upper-tier racked stock (above declared flood mark): largely unaffected, still being temperature-audited for cold-chain breach duration 4. ESTIMATED CLAIM AMOUNT

4. ESTIMATED CLAIM AMOUNT Buildings (cold hall, loading bay, lobby): KES 18,500,000 Plant and Machinery (refrigeration, electrics): KES 27,000,000 Stock (spoiled / contaminated foodstuffs): KES 44,500,000 Clean-up, drying, and temporary cold hire (est.): KES 2,000,000 --------------------------------------------------------------- Total Claimed: KES 92,000,000 5. SUPPORTING DOCUMENTS ENCLOSED [X] Copy of Policy Schedule [X] Photographs of inundation and debris (38 images) [X] Kenya Meteorological Department rainfall summary for Nairobi, 14–15 April 2026 [ ] Independent flood investigation / loss adjuster report - NOT YET RECEIVED, instructed 16 April 2026, expected within 10 working days [X] Stock inventory extract as at 13 April 2026 [ ] Final stock reconciliation after write-off - PARTIALLY PROVIDED [ ] Drainage clearance / maintenance log for Q1 2026 - REQUESTED, NOT YET RECEIVED [X] Statement from night supervisor (Ms. Amina Otieno) [X] List of previous claims under this Policy (see Section 6) [ ] Invoices for refrigeration plant claimed as damaged - PARTIALLY PROVIDED 6. PREVIOUS CLAIMS UNDER THIS POLICY (as declared by Insured)

6. PREVIOUS CLAIMS UNDER THIS POLICY (as declared by Insured) - May 2024: Surface-water ingress after blocked drain; claimed KES 4,200,000; settled KES 3,600,000. - November 2025: Storm water under loading-bay doors; claimed KES 6,800,000; settled KES 5,900,000. - No other claims declared in the preceding 5 years. 7. INSURED'S DECLARATION I confirm that the information given above is true to the best of my knowledge.
I understand that the Insurer's liability is subject to the terms, conditions,
exclusions and warranties of the Policy. Signed: D. Mwangi (Operations Director, Kariobangi Cold Storage & Logistics Limited)
Date: 16 April 2026 8. INTERNAL NOTE - AMANI GENERAL INSURANCE CLAIMS DEPARTMENT

Signed: D. Mwangi (Operations Director, Kariobangi Cold Storage & Logistics Limited)
Date: 16 April 2026 8. INTERNAL NOTE - AMANI GENERAL INSURANCE CLAIMS DEPARTMENT Given the estimated gross loss of KES 92,000,000, this claim falls above the
Cedant's retention of KES 50,000,000 under Treaty KR/AGI/FLD/SUR/2026 and has been
notified to Kenya Reinsurance Corporation Limited on 17 April 2026, within the
14-day notification period. Flood investigation report and drainage-maintenance
records are outstanding. Applicability of Warranty 1 (drainage) and Warranty 2
(elevated storage / flood mark) is not yet confirmed. Underwriting file notes that
this risk is an Enhanced Assessment Risk under Article 3 (sum insured and Kariobangi
hotspot corridor). Portfolio CAT desk shows Eastlands locations with elevated
susceptibility under moderate-to-severe return-period tiers for the same catchment.

INDEPENDENT FLOOD INVESTIGATION REPORT Prepared by: Ridgeway Loss Adjusters & Assessors Ltd
Report Reference: RWA/FLD/2026/0412
For: Amani General Insurance Company Limited
Re: Kariobangi Cold Storage & Logistics Limited - Plot 7, Outer Ring Road, Kariobangi South, Nairobi
Claim Reference: AGI/CLM/2026/2048
Date of Report: 28 April 2026
Date of Site Inspection: 18 April 2026 1. INSTRUCTIONS We were instructed by Amani General Insurance Company Limited to attend the site,
investigate the cause and mechanism of the flood loss of 14–15 April 2026, and to
comment on the extent of loss and the condition of flood-mitigation measures
(drainage clearance and elevated storage / flood mark) at the time of the incident. 2. FINDINGS - CAUSE AND MECHANISM

2.1 Physical evidence and neighbour statements confirm that intense overnight rainfall produced widespread surface-water ponding along Outer Ring Road and the Kariobangi South drainage corridor on 14–15 April 2026. This is consistent with known Eastlands pluvial hotspots (Kariobangi, Dandora, and adjacent catchments) used in Kenya Re's Nairobi flood desk hotspot list.
2.2 Water entered the Insured's yard primarily from the roadside storm-water channel adjacent to the loading bay. At inspection we found the channel heavily silted, with solid waste and packaging debris obstructing the culvert inlet serving the site frontage. Water marks on the loading-bay walls indicate peak external depth of approximately 50–55 cm above yard level.
2.3 Inside the main cold-room hall, water marks and silt lines indicate peak inundation of approximately 38 cm above finished floor level — above the Policy's declared flood mark of 0.45 m only in the sense that stock on the lowest tier (stored at roughly 0.15–0.20 m above floor on pallets) was fully immersed; the declared warranty requires lowest storage not less than 0.45 m.
2.4 In our professional opinion, the most probable cause is accidental pluvial / urban flood arising from extreme rainfall combined with inadequate local

2.4 In our professional opinion, the most probable cause is accidental pluvial / urban flood arising from extreme rainfall combined with inadequate local drainage conveyance at the site frontage. We found no evidence of deliberate diversion of water onto the premises by a third party. We cannot entirely exclude contribution from upstream public-system surcharge, but site-level blockage materially increased the depth and duration of inundation on this risk.
3. FINDINGS - FLOOD MITIGATION AND WARRANTIES

3.1 Drainage clearance (Warranty 1): We requested Q1 2026 drainage clearance / maintenance logs required under Warranty 1(a). At inspection, the Insured produced only an informal WhatsApp instruction to a casual labourer dated February 2026; no dated photographic log or contractor invoice for the mandatory 90-day clearance cycle covering March–April 2026 was available. The obstructed culvert inlet and silted channel are, in our view, consistent with lack of recent clearance and are more likely than not to have increased the depth of water entering the loading bay.
3.2 Temporary flood defences (Warranty 1(b)): A small store of sandbags was present but partially degraded and not pre-positioned at the loading-bay doors when the Kenya Meteorological Department heavy-rainfall advisory for Nairobi was issued on the afternoon of 14 April 2026. Staff placed bags after water was already rising — too late to prevent entry.
3.3 Elevated storage / flood mark (Warranty 2): Ground-tier pallets of frozen foodstuffs were stored with base height approximately 0.15–0.20 m above floor level, below the 0.45 m declared flood mark. Upper racking above ~0.50 m was largely dry. Stock loss is concentrated on the non-compliant lower tiers. Plant motors mounted at floor level in the plant room were similarly below

largely dry. Stock loss is concentrated on the non-compliant lower tiers. Plant motors mounted at floor level in the plant room were similarly below any elevated mounting that might have limited electrical damage.
3.4 We are not qualified to opine on the legal effect of any warranty breach; that is a matter for the Insurer's claims and legal assessment. We can confirm that the drainage and storage deficiencies noted above are, in our professional opinion, more likely than not to have contributed to the extent of the loss.

4. ESTIMATED EXTENT OF LOSS (Adjuster's Preliminary Assessment) Buildings (cold hall flooring/panels, loading bay, lobby): Adjuster estimate: KES 16,200,000 Plant and Machinery (refrigeration motors, switchgear, damaged racking): Adjuster estimate: KES 23,500,000 Stock (spoiled / contaminated — lower tiers; upper tiers mostly salvageable): Adjuster estimate, pending final write-off reconciliation: KES 38,000,000 to 41,000,000 Clean-up, drying, temporary cold hire: Adjuster estimate: KES 1,800,000 --------------------------------------------------------------------------- Preliminary Adjuster Estimate (Total): KES 79,500,000 to 82,500,000 This preliminary estimate is below the Insured's claimed figure of KES 92,000,000,
principally due to differences in assessed stock write-off on upper tiers and
plant salvage assumptions, pending final reconciliation. 5. OBSERVATIONS RELEVANT TO POLICY WARRANTIES

5. OBSERVATIONS RELEVANT TO POLICY WARRANTIES We note for the Insurer's consideration that the apparent lapse in drainage
clearance (Warranty 1) and storage below the declared flood mark (Warranty 2)
may be relevant to warranty compliance and to any reduction of indemnity. The
loss itself is assessed as a genuine flood event; the open questions are extent
and warranty application, not whether flooding occurred. 6. RECOMMENDATIONS 1. Obtain contractor invoices / dated photographic logs for drainage clearance covering January–April 2026, or confirm their absence. 2. Finalise stock write-off against the 13 April inventory and temperature logs. 3. Obtain asset-register / invoice support for refrigeration plant claimed. 4. Consider Kenya Re referral under Treaty Article 6 given gross loss above KES 60,000,000, outstanding documentation, and warranty doubt. 5. We consider the claim, subject to the above outstanding items and the Insurer's assessment of warranty compliance, to be a genuine pluvial flood loss arising from the April 2026 Eastlands rainfall event. Prepared by: S. Mutiso, Senior Loss Adjuster, Ridgeway Loss Adjusters & Assessors Ltd
